btos.label: Mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction (NAICS 21)

name: Mining
blurb: Autonomous haulage and ore-body modelling in the sector that automated early, from USGS exploration data and Earth MRI to Rio Tinto, Komatsu, KoBold, and the AI-native explorers.

summary: Autonomous haulage and ore-body modelling are the established deployments in a sector that adopted automation early. Mining AI splits into two horizons: exploration - long-term forecasting from satellite, magnetic, and core-scan data toward drilling targets - and site operations, where sensor streams and telemetry drive machinery, maintenance, and safety minute by minute.

analysis.body:
The Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey puts AI use in mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction at 13.0% of firms in the latest period, up from 8.0% in the prior period. That is a measured figure, drawn directly from firms rather than estimated, and it makes mining one of the sectors where adoption can be tracked over time rather than inferred. The survey asks whether the business used AI in the last two weeks, so the number reflects active use, not experimentation or intent.

What the sources show being deployed splits into two layers. The first is equipment: Komatsu, one of the dominant mining equipment makers, publishes autonomous haulage and fleet management technology, and describes an industry on the cusp of rapid change where advanced automation and integrated technologies intersect, including a strategic partnership with AIM Intelligent Machines for autonomous operation of bulldozers and hydraulic excavators. Rio Tinto's own automation program, autonomous haul trucks and drills operating at scale, is the primary-source record of what day-to-day operational AI looks like in production mining. This is where operational AI ships as machinery rather than software.

The second layer is geology and processing. GeologicAI combines high-fidelity data, robust analytics, and domain expertise across the mining cycle, using multi-sensor core scanning with RGB, XRF, hyperspectral, and LiDAR, and states that Agnico Eagle uses its scanning services to make more confident decisions. Freeport-McMoRan applies machine learning to processing, maximizing mill throughput and ore recovery at existing operations rather than finding new ones. KoBold Metals describes finding the materials of the future with AI and HI, and its Mingomba project in Zambia, one of the world's largest copper mines, is the sector's clearest AI-native bet. Newmont's own pages are cited as the record for AI in drill-core analysis, predictive maintenance, and automated safety monitoring among the major gold miners.

The public data layer underneath all of this comes from the U.S. Geological Survey. Its Mineral Resources Program is the authoritative source of mineral resource information, including statistics on mineral production, trade, and supply chain risks, and the National Mineral Information Center is described as the authoritative source in that area. Earth MRI, the Earth Mapping Resources Initiative, is modernizing mapping of the nation's surface and subsurface, delivering high-quality data to understand geology and find new critical and other mineral resources. The sourced points describe this as the dataset behind machine-learning prospectivity work on critical minerals.

On standards and policy, the National Mining Association is the official voice of U.S. mining, advocating before Congress, federal agencies, the judiciary, and the media, and tracking regulatory change and technology adoption across American operations. The International Council on Mining and Metals works on a safe, just and sustainable world enabled by responsibly produced minerals and metals, and its materials cover social performance, a 2025 safety report with transparent data on fatalities, injuries, and workplace hazards, water stress mapping, a greenhouse gas emissions dataset, and a tailings progress report on implementing the Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management. The Society for Mining, Metallurgy and Exploration is described as carrying the working-group research on AI, machine learning, and automation in mineral processing.

The excerpts do not report ROI figures, cost savings, or failure rates for AI in this sector, and they do not quantify vendor market share or investment totals, so those questions are left open here. What a reader deciding whether to deploy should take from the material is narrower but concrete: the measured adoption base is still small, the proven deployments cluster around autonomous equipment, core scanning, and mill optimization at large operators, the underlying geologic data is publicly anchored by USGS and Earth MRI, and the standards and safety expectations that any deployment must fit within are set by bodies like ICMM and NMA.

https://www.icmm.com/.brief: ICMM is a leadership organization working for a “safe, just and sustainable world” enabled by responsibly produced minerals and metals. It reports that its 2025 safety report provides transparent data on fatalities, injuries and workplace hazards, and its 2025 Tax Contribution Report shows members paid a higher share of earnings to society despite lower profits. The organization also publishes a new Global Mining & Metals GHG Emissions Dataset, maps water stress risks around mining facilities, and highlights water as a missing piece in the energy transition through Emma Gagen’s blog. Recent announcements include the appointment of Iván Arriagada as Chair, James Clark as Director of Communications and External Affairs, and the release of the Tailings Progress Report on GISTM implementation, while a documentary on the World’s Deepest Marathon showcases responsible mining practices.

https://www.smenet.org/.brief: The Society for Mining, Metallurgy and Exploration (SME) presents itself as a “world leader” in sharing information and networking for engineers working in mining and metallurgy. It states that its focus is on engineering-related professionals in those fields. SME is also listed as a member society of OneMine, the SME Foundation, and the American Institute of Mining, Metallurgical, and Petroleum Engineers (AIME). The page ends with a 2026 copyright notice.

https://www.newmont.com/.brief: Newmont offers university students and recent graduates opportunities to gain “real-world experience” with a global mining leader. The site provides a subscription service that delivers updates on financial news, press releases, upcoming events and presentations, performance reports, blog posts, and more. Users can receive these updates directly to their inbox.

https://www.geologicai.com/.brief: GeologicAI claims it offers tools, technologies, and solutions that let mining companies make critical decisions with confidence. The company says it is the only one that combines high-fidelity data, robust analytics, and domain expertise at every stage of the mining cycle, providing core scanning, core logging, and resource modeling. Its multi-sensor core scanning uses RGB, XRF, hyperspectral, and LiDAR to deliver accurate, consistent datasets with a low-effort delivery model. The Digital Core Table supplies reliable data and AI tools to improve logging consistency and efficiency, freeing geologists to focus on interpretation. Agnico Eagle has adopted the scanning services to support more confident decisions across its mining cycle.

https://www.koboldmetals.com/.brief: The site states that the Mingomba project in Zambia is expected to become one of the world’s largest copper mines. It notes that the development is being carried out by a local Zambian team. The focus is on using AI and high-intensity methods to discover future-materials.

https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/eart.brief: Earth MRI is modernizing mapping of the nation’s surface and subsurface, delivering high-quality data to help understand geology, locate critical mineral resources, and guide national decisions. Julia A. McIntosh and colleagues report that Hicks Dome breccias in Illinois are enriched in rare earth elements, Y, Th, F, Ba, Ti, Nb, and Be, and are associated with lamprophyre dikes dated to about 271 Ma; the study also notes that Hicks Dome lies within the Illinois, Kentucky Fluorspar District, which hosts fluorite, lead-zinc, and barite resources. Earth MRI released an update on research in Montana’s Boulder Batholith region, focusing on critical minerals in zinc ore. The initiative is expanding its coverage with high-resolution airborne radiometric surveys that reveal unseen geology, mineral potential, and possible health hazards.

https://www.usgs.gov/programs/mineral-re.brief: The USGS Mineral Resources Program describes itself as the nation's primary source of scientific information on the full life cycle and supply chains of mineral resources, including critical minerals. It says the Earth Mapping Resources Initiative is modernizing mapping of the nation's geology and critical mineral resources, and that the National Mineral Information Center serves as an authoritative source of mineral resource information, including statistics on production, trade and supply chain risks. The program also offers lesson plans, activities, infographics and fact sheets tied to its science. Two research items are listed: a study of trace element heterogeneity and crystallization history in Plesovice zircon and its implications for use as a reference material, and a study of how mineral deposit data affects predictions from a three-part approach to quantitative mineral resource assessment, drawing on 16 previous USGS assessments.
